business_problem: Agility Robotics needed a reliable way to train whole-body control for humanoid robots that could work in human-built warehouses and factories without costly facility redesigns or risky trial-and-error learning on the production floor.
solution_summary: Agility Robotics built a simulation-first training stack for Digit by combining NVIDIA Isaac Sim, Isaac Lab, NVIDIA Omniverse, OpenUSD, and GPU-accelerated reinforcement learning. Engineers model Digit's chassis and contact surfaces in Isaac Sim, then ingest customer CAD and BIM data into shared OpenUSD scenes that capture aisle widths, floor friction, lighting, and shove forces. These digital-twin scenarios flow into Isaac Lab, where millions of parallel reinforcement-learning episodes train a whole-body controller on NVIDIA GPUs and keep perception tightly coupled with motion planning. Agility then validates the same policy in a containerized MuJoCo pipeline to expose simulator-specific corner cases before deployment to real robot hardware. This end-to-end workflow lets Digit learn balance recovery, obstacle avoidance, and material-handling behavior in simulation so trained controllers transfer into live warehouse and manufacturing operations without lengthy manual retuning.

solution_components.name: NVIDIA Isaac Sim
solution_components.role: Hosts the physics-based robot and facility simulations used to model Digit and its operating environments.

solution_components.name: Isaac Lab
solution_components.role: Runs large-scale reinforcement-learning training to refine Digit's whole-body control policies.

solution_components.name: NVIDIA Omniverse
solution_components.role: Provides the simulation platform foundation for Agility's digital-twin training workflows.

solution_components.name: OpenUSD
solution_components.role: Keeps robot geometry, joint data, and customer facility models in a shared scene graph for simulation.

solution_components.name: NVIDIA GPUs
solution_components.role: Supply the accelerated compute needed for billions of simulation interactions and fast controller training.

solution_components.name: MuJoCo
solution_components.role: Serves as a second, containerized physics environment to validate policies against simulator-specific corner cases.

data_flow: Robot geometry plus customer CAD and BIM data are modeled in Isaac Sim and OpenUSD scenes, simulation episodes flow into Isaac Lab for GPU-accelerated reinforcement learning, validated policies are cross-checked in MuJoCo, and the resulting controllers are deployed onto Digit robots in warehouse and manufacturing environments.
business_outcome: Agility Robotics cut controller iteration cycles from weeks to days, trained Digit across billions of simulated interactions, and transferred whole-body control policies from digital twins into live warehouse and manufacturing operations with better stability, higher reliability, and faster deployment readiness.
metrics: years of real-world learning for Digit in just hours
